title: 2026 Mustang Dark Horse SC First Drive: Power Chord
summary: When my feet flew off the passenger-side carpet under 1.5 g for the second time, I began to realize how much of Ford’s new-for-2026 Mustang Dark Horse SC I had not experienced during my own brief session behind the wheel. body_markdown:
When my feet flew off the passenger-side carpet under 1.5 g for the second time, I began to realize how much of Ford’s new-for-2026 Mustang Dark Horse SC I had not experienced during my own brief session behind the wheel. In the driver seat was Ford vehicle dynamics engineer and SCCA national champion Steve Thompson. The tires squealed intermittently as he adjusted the steering angle, dancing with the car as it hurtled through the rollercoaster that is Sonoma Raceway. That evening, I found my collarbones were red from being thrown against the five-point harness (in a seat clearly not designed for five-foot-six women). To be clear: I was having a lot of fun.


The newest model in a proliferating lineup of pony cars, the Dark Horse SC is the most track-focused Mustang that rolls off an assembly line. (The[limited-production, $325,000 GTD](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2025-mustang-gtd-first-drive-true-to-its-roots/) does not roll off the assembly line at Flat Rock, Michigan, as a finished product, and is not available to the general public; you must apply to purchase one.) After a day with the SC, on road and on track, I found this 795-horsepower, supercharged Mustang both astoundingly capable and surprisingly approachable.


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


The Dark Horse SC riffs on a formula you’ll recognize from the[2020–22 Shelby GT500](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/track-tested-ford-shelby-gt500-vs-porsche-cayman-gt4-4-0/) : supercharged 5.2-liter “Predator” V-8, seven-speed TREMEC dual-clutch transmission, Torsen rear differential, lots of brake and tire. The Shelby name disappeared from Ford’s lineup along with that car, likely because Ford tired of paying licensing fees to Shelby American. Ford’s expanding racing ambitions spelled the end of the partnership, anyway, in our eyes. After all, why would Ford race Mustangs on Sunday so Shelby could sell GT500s on Monday? The Dark Horse debuted in 2022 as part of the Mustang’s seventh (S650) generation, and four years later, the nameplate is its own subgenre, complete with[a one-make race series starring the Dark Horse R](https://www.hagerty.com/media/motorsports/ford-sent-40-horses-to-le-mans-for-mustang-challenge-euro-debut/) . With the SC, that subgenre has its own halo model.


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


Differentiated from the 5.0-liter Dark Horse by over 300 parts, the Dark Horse SC is available in three flavors: regular, Track Pack, and the limited-run Track Pack Special Edition. On-road, I chose the “regular” Dark Horse SC ($108,085, including destination and gas guzzler tax). The tester carried $10,000 in painted graphics, plus another $395 for fancy seatbelts, plus a one-year subscription for wifi, audio, and voice assistant, bringing its total to $119,225. For the track sessions, I had one choice: the Dark Horse SC Track Pack ($147,185 with destination and gas guzzler tax), which boasts carbon-fiber wheels shod in Michelin Pilot Sport Cup2 R tires, carbon-ceramic brakes borrowed from the GTD, a ducktail spoiler, and a unique MagneRide calibration.


## Specs: 2026 Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC


**Base Price:** $108,085 / $119,225
**Powertrain:** 5.2-liter, supercharged, cross-plane V-8
**Output:** 795 hp @ 7200 rpm, 660 lb-ft of torque @ 4600 rpm
**Layout:** front-engine, rear-wheel-drive, two-door, four-seat coupe
**Weight:** 4263 pounds
**0–60 mph:** TBA
**EPA-rated Fuel Economy:** TBA
**Competitors:** Chevrolet Corvette Z06


The Dark Horse SC is not the only way to get a supercharged Mustang, but it is the most complete way, says Carl Widmann, the personable, white-haired boss of Ford Racing production vehicles. The other way is via the Ford Racing Parts catalog, which offers an $18,500 package that includes a Whipple Gen 6 supercharger, a cat-back exhaust, and a host of chassis bits. ([We drove a Mustang so equipped earlier this year, in Michigan.](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/factory-tuned-we-drive-fords-800-hp-mustang-700-hp-f-150-and-300-hp-maverick/) ) However, says Widmann, such a modified Mustang is not an electronically integrated solution. To further prove his point, he references the SC’s aero package (it represents 12,000 hours of computational fluid dynamics work), the model-specific tires that took two years to develop, the engine durability testing, and 140 hours of wind-tunnel aero testing. The car that we drove in Michigan, he says, represents more of a “statement piece.”


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)

It’s a rough life, being a prototype part.


Developed alongside the GT4 and GTD Mustang at racetracks across the U.S., the SC benefits from the tools and methods as the race cars. Its Predator V-8 did 24-hour durability sessions using the same dyno cell that Ford used to test[the 5.4-liter V-8 in its LMDh race car](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/hear-fords-le-mans-hypercar-crank-to-life/) , which is bound for the 24 Hours of Le Mans next year. Arie Groeneveld, chief engineer for the SC, said that collaboration with Ford’s NASCAR teams yielded a more efficient iterative process for the car’s hood. (It boasts a giant vent that both extracts heat and helps reduce front-end lift.) Instead of mocking up a new hood to test incremental differences, they told Ford’s production-car team, why don’t you divide the hood into many different panels and change one panel at a time? It’s a testament to how Ford sees the SC that the 2027 NASCAR Cup Series stock car will carry a new redesign[and the SC name](https://www.nascar.com/news-media/2026/01/16/ford-racing-mustang-dark-horse-sc-set-for-2027-nascar-season/) .


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


How does the personality of the Dark Horse SC compare to that of its predecessor, the GT500? Though the two cars share a “familial resemblance,” the Dark Horse SC represents “incremental but significant” change, says Thompson. He would know; he tuned the chassis of both cars (and served as development driver on the GTD program, too). The Dark Horse SC is firmer than the GT500, with stiffer swaybars and springs. The front wheels are wider, too: 11.5 inches compared to 11. Largely because of that change, the front aluminum knuckles are new, and unique to the SC. Where the GT500 used third-gen MagneRide dampers, the SC uses fourth-gen units, primarily differentiated by software. Ford worked with BWI, which makes the magneto-rheological (MR) dampers, to create road algorithms and allow for more flexibility in how they can tune the dampers for low- versus high-speed impacts. The tune of the MR dampers is different for the Track Pack, allowing for 25% lower unsprung weight compared to a Dark Horse and yielding “a bit better transitions across center.”


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)

Thompson stressed how much Ford wants the Dark Horse SC to be approachable by both the novice and the veteran track driver. “I want people with minimal amounts of experience to get in and come out and say, ‘Hey, you know what? That was less intimidating to me than I thought it was going to be.'”


Count your author among such people. On the quarter-mile drag-strip at Sonoma, the Dark Horse SC stuck like snot and pulled like a freight train. On the track, it was highly tolerant: No matter how tentatively I approached a turn, braking and turning in too late, adjusting my angle mid-corner, the SC didn’t care. After the second session, I realized that I was more intimidated by the track than the car. It had more power, more grip, and more brakes than I could use. Fail to carry speed through a corner? Just squeeze the right pedal. I tried braking incrementally later, each lap, for the hairpin that is Turn 11, and over-braked. The pedal is linear and progressive—I was well aware I had pressed relatively slowly and, had I stomped on it, could have yanked myself to a stop in much less time. As I snaked uphill through Turns 2 through 4, I added throttle while the wheel wasn’t straight, but the traction control realized it would be unwise to fulfill my request and cut power. Configurable in one of five levels, from most to least restrictive, it’s a key ingredient in making the car accessible to a variety of skill levels. The one I was using, Thompson said, was “very first-timer friendly.”


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


It is remarkable that the SC does not punish the novice for being a novice. That said, it is hard to learn from a car whose limits are as far beyond yours as the SC’s were from mine. A car with less power, less grip, less weight and brakes—and a lower ceiling—will talk to you more, both when you do something right and when you do something wrong. The SC began to talk to me once, in my very brief time on-track with it, in a carousel left-hander: As the car pressed down and out of Turn 6, a blind-entry carousel left-hander that slings the car uphill, I fed more and more power as I unwound the wheel, feeling the steering begin to tense up slightly as the V-8 roared.


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)

Some “carbon fiber” trim…


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


… and the real deal, just below it.


[Grace Jarvis](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/grace-jarvis/)


On the road, the SC is surprisingly comfortable. It’s even quiet, if you avoid the active exhaust’s loudest mode and restrain your right foot from asking for More of the Good Noises, Please. Road noise is well suppressed thanks to an active noise cancellation system borrowed from the regular Mustang convertibles. On non-Track Pack cars, equipped with Pirelli P Zero tires, foam pads inside the tires help tamp down tire roar. Thicker interior carpet laid on top of a special foam layer also contributes. The additional layer added weight, Ford told us, but the NVH argument won out. The only obvious shortcoming in the SC’s cabin is in the materials: No car of this caliber or price should have plastic shift paddles or fake carbon fiber—much less, next to real carbon fiber. Customizability is important at this price point, and Ford is on the right track with the optional teal brake calipers and the colorful seatbelt options, but the few faux finishes in the interior are, as they say, “opportunities for growth.”


With the Dark Horse SC, Ford has adapted the GT500’s formula to fit its own purposes, a strong indication that the carmaker knows what it’s about and doesn’t need to reinvent an already-excellent package. Indeed, it is impressive that an old-school, brawny muscle car like the SC exists in 2026. “It’s only going to be around for a while before it plays itself out,” says Widmann. If the Dark Horse SC sings your kind of music, it’s time to join the party.


## 2026 Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC


**Highs:** Hugely powerful engine and brakes, accommodating on-road, tolerant on-track personality
**Lows:** A few faux interior materials
**Summary:** Ford’s latest reprisal of the supercharged Mustang theme is easy to love.
